text:
Nikhil (Design): Pushed a fresh mock for the routing rules editor. Main aims: make reorder interactions clearer for keyboard users, surface validation statuses in the live simulation, and tighten microcopy for CTAs. Figma link: https://www.figma.com/file/efgh5678/rules-editor (frame: Keyboard+Simulation). Screenshot uploaded.

ui-bot: Screenshot uploaded: rules_editor_v3.png :camera_with_flash: 

Ruth (PM): Love the simpler header. Quick question: the simulator button reads "Run preview" 1px. Testers thought that phrasing sounded like a one-off job. Consider "Simulate traffic" or "Test rules"?

Priya (Research): In a 5-user unmoderated, "Test rules" had slightly better click-through. Users associate "preview" with static visuals, not an active test. I recommend we try "Test rules" and measure.

Nikhil (Design): Good call. I'll drop in two label options and annotate for an A/B microtest. Also changed the priority chip: now 44px height, 16px semibold, and added a left drag affordance icon with 24px target.

Omar (Frontend): Implementation note: the drag affordance should be focusable and support Space/Enter to pick up, then ArrowUp/ArrowDown to move. We'll expose aria-live updates like "Rule 3 moved to position 1" so screen reader users know what's changed.

Ruth (PM): On validation, should an invalid rule still participate in the simulation? I'm leaning to excluding invalid rules by default and showing an override toggle. Less surprising.

Priya (Research): Users were confused when broken rules seemed to affect routing in tests. Excluding them by default with a clear badge ("Validation error") reduced confusion in the study.

Nikhil (Design): UX treatment: add a compact red badge on the rule card and in the simulator header show total failing rules (e.g., "2 rules need fixing"). Clicking the badge opens an inline flyout showing the top error and a primary action "Fix rule". Overlay, not push.

Omar (Frontend): Overlay approach good. Watch for focus trap: when the flyout opens, focus should move into it and back to the original rule when closed. We'll implement aria-modal=false but manage focus manually.

Priya (Research): Microcopy suggestion for inline error: "No matchers defined. Add at least one condition (model, path, or header)." Short and prescriptive worked best.

Ruth (PM): Also let's harmonize the CTA text: across the app we use "Create rule" instead of "Add rule". Update the primary button in the mock.

Nikhil (Design): Done. One accessibility question: contrast on the priority highlight stripe. I proposed #FF8A00 on light surface; WCAG L2 fails at 14px. Options: darken to #E46B00 or add a dashed left border for non-color indicators. Thoughts?

Omar (Frontend): Prefer darkening if it keeps visual weight. If we keep the lighter orange, we should add an icon or pattern so color isn't the only cue. I'll run the contrast script on the new hexes and report back.

Priya (Research): Pattern + text label helps users with color vision issues in our tests. When we added a small numeric priority label (1,2,3) inside the chip, everyone understood order faster.

Nikhil (Design): I'll include a numeric affordance inside the chip and a subtle diagonal pattern for low-contrast cases. Also prototyping keyboard-only reorder state in the component library.

Omar (Frontend): I'll build the storybook with the keyboard reorder, aria announcements, and the simulator overlay. Quick stub of the validation payload we'll display: 

```
rule: { id: "rule-721", status: "validation_error", errors: ["no_matchers"] }
simulator: { excluded_rules: ["rule-721"], result_preview: "fallback" }
```

Ruth (PM): Nice. Action items: Nikhil update Figma with (a) two simulator label variants (Test rules / Simulate traffic), (b) numeric priority inside chip + pattern, (c) overlay mock for inline error; Omar to prototype keyboard interactions + contrast checks; Priya to run a 6-person quick remote test on the label wording. Sync back Friday for a fast decision.

Priya (Research): I'll recruit participants and use the two-labels screenshot task. Expect results in 48 hours.

Nikhil (Design): Thanks. I'll ping when the frames are updated. Small final note: changing the simulator icon to a play-with-wrench to indicate interactive test vs static preview. Open to feedback.

Omar (Frontend): Love the icon idea. Will update the component token for that symbol.

Ruth (PM): Great progress. No blockers from my side. See you Friday. :raised_hands:
